description: Discovering, analysing, specifying, validating and managing what a software system must do: stakeholder analysis and elicitation, functional and non-functional requirements, use cases and user stories, requirements models, prioritisation and negotiation, traceability, and requirements for users with poor connectivity. Students practise on simulated stakeholder interviews and case studies in the browser, producing and reviewing a complete requirements specification for a real local problem.
modelledOn: Robertson and Robertson, Mastering the Requirements Process
ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 Systems and Software Engineering: Requirements Engineering
IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide)
outcomes: Identify and analyse stakeholders and plan and conduct elicitation with interviews, observation, workshops and prototypes.
Write clear, testable functional and non-functional requirements and organise them into a specification that follows ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148.
Express requirements as use cases, user stories with acceptance criteria and analysis models.
Validate, prioritise and negotiate requirements among stakeholders with conflicting goals.
Manage change and maintain traceability from business goals to requirements, design and tests.
Design requirements that account for low connectivity, low-end devices, local languages and varied literacy.

units.title: Requirements and the requirements process
topics: What a requirement is: business, user and system requirements; requirements versus design
The requirements engineering process: elicitation, analysis, specification, validation and management
Why projects fail on requirements; the cost of requirements errors
Requirements in plan-driven and agile development
Running case: a mobile money agent and float-management app

units.title: Stakeholders and elicitation techniques
topics: Identifying stakeholders: the onion model, power-interest grids, user classes and personas
Interviews: structured, semi-structured and unstructured; question design and active listening
Observation and ethnography; apprenticing and contextual inquiry
Workshops, focus groups, questionnaires, document analysis and prototyping
Tacit knowledge, elicitation pitfalls and working through interpreters in multilingual communities
Simulated interviews with district health officers about routine health data reporting

units.title: Functional and non-functional requirements
topics: Functional requirements, business rules, constraints and data requirements
Qualities of a good requirement: correct, unambiguous, complete, consistent, verifiable, traceable
Non-functional requirements and the ISO/IEC 25010 quality model
Quantifying qualities with fit criteria and Planguage
Detecting and removing ambiguity; requirement templates and boilerplates

units.title: Use cases and user stories
topics: Actors, goals and use case diagrams; include and extend relationships
Fully dressed use cases: main success scenario, alternative and exception flows, pre- and post-conditions
User stories and the INVEST criteria; epics, themes and splitting stories
Acceptance criteria in Given-When-Then form
Story mapping and building a product backlog
Writing use cases and stories for buying a tro-tro ticket by mobile money

units.title: Requirements modelling
topics: Context diagrams, event lists and data flow diagrams
Domain models with class diagrams; entity-relationship models
Behaviour models: state machines, activity diagrams and BPMN process models
Goal-oriented modelling with i* and KAOS
Formal specification in brief: why and when to use Alloy or Z
Modelling the cocoa purchasing chain from farmer to buying company to port

units.title: Validation, prioritisation and negotiation
topics: Validation techniques: reviews, inspections, walkthroughs and checklists
Prototyping and acceptance tests as validation; testability of requirements
Prioritisation: MoSCoW, Kano model, cost-value analysis and the analytic hierarchy process
Negotiation and conflict resolution; the WinWin approach
Estimating size and effort from requirements
Simulated review meeting with stakeholders who disagree

units.title: Requirements management and traceability
topics: Baselines, versioning and change control; the change control board and impact analysis
Traceability: forward and backward links, the traceability matrix
Requirements tools and attributes: status, priority, source, rationale
Structure of a software requirements specification following ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148
Requirements volatility and measuring requirements quality

units.title: Requirements for low-connectivity users
topics: Offline-first requirements: local storage, synchronisation, conflict resolution and data costs
Channels beyond the smartphone: USSD, SMS and voice for feature-phone users
Device, battery and power-cut constraints as non-functional requirements
Localisation into Twi, Ewe, Hausa and other local languages; designing for varied literacy
Accessibility requirements and WCAG
Field validation in low-bandwidth settings

units.title: Security, privacy, safety and the capstone
topics: Security requirements, misuse cases and abuse cases
Privacy requirements and Ghana's Data Protection Act; consent and data minimisation
Safety-critical and regulated systems: hazards and safety requirements
Capstone: a validated, traceable requirements specification for a local organisation

schedule.title: Foundations of requirements engineering
schedule.exercise: Sort 12 statements from a project brief into business, user and system requirements, and flag which are really design decisions.

tasks.title: Classify 15 statements as business, user or system requirements, or as design choices, and compare with the rubric's answers
Draw the requirements process as a BPMN diagram with elicitation, analysis, specification, validation and management and their outputs
Review a failed project case, find which requirement errors caused rework, estimate their cost and recommend three early checks

schedule.title: Stakeholders and interviews
schedule.exercise: Write ten interview questions for a mobile money agent, mixing open and closed, and mark any that lead the answer.

tasks.title: Draw an onion model and a power-interest grid for a mobile money agent app, placing at least 10 stakeholders
Interview a simulated agent about float shortages, choose questions at each turn and list the needs you uncovered
Run a contextual inquiry at a simulated market stall, record observations against stated needs and identify three tacit requirements

schedule.title: More elicitation techniques
schedule.exercise: Prepare a workshop agenda and a short questionnaire for gathering requirements from clinic staff in two languages.

tasks.title: Pick the best elicitation technique for 6 situations such as many users, hidden practice or early vision, and justify each choice
Conduct an interview through an interpreter in a branching case, avoid leading questions and score the accuracy of the notes you take
Interview district health officers about routine reporting, uncover pain points and conflicting needs and write 10 candidate requirements with sources

schedule.title: Writing good requirements
schedule.exercise: Rewrite ten vague statements such as 'fast' and 'user friendly' as measurable requirements with a fit criterion.

tasks.title: Find the ambiguity in 12 requirement sentences, mark the vague words and rewrite each using a template
Convert eight non-functional wishes into Planguage requirements with scale, meter, must and plan levels, and have them scored
Draw a quality tree from ISO 25010 for a wallet app, attach measurable fit criteria to six leaves and mark conflicts between them

schedule.title: Use cases and user stories
schedule.exercise: Write a fully dressed use case for withdrawing cash at an agent, with two exception flows and the post-conditions.

tasks.title: Draw a use case diagram for a school fees payment app with four actors and six use cases, using include and extend correctly
Write a fully dressed use case with main success scenario, three alternative flows and pre- and post-conditions for a customer cash-in
Split an epic into user stories that meet INVEST, spot the five stories that fail it and rewrite them, then be scored against the rubric

schedule.title: Acceptance criteria and backlogs
schedule.exercise: Write Given-When-Then criteria for a tro-tro ticket purchase with insufficient funds and a network timeout.

tasks.title: Write Given-When-Then criteria for four user stories and check each is testable and free of design detail
Build a story map of the buying journey for tro-tro tickets and cut a first release slice with a clear goal
Produce a use case diagram, one detailed use case, six user stories and acceptance criteria for buying a tro-tro ticket by mobile money

schedule.title: Models of the system
schedule.exercise: Explain which model you would use to show data stored, process flow and state changes for a loan application and why.

tasks.title: Draw a context diagram and level-1 data flow diagram for a clinic appointment system with at least five processes and stores
Model the entities of a mobile money agent app as a class or entity-relationship diagram with correct multiplicities and attributes
Model a loan approval process as BPMN with exceptions and a state machine of the loan's states, checking both for consistency

schedule.title: Goals, formal specs and value chains
schedule.exercise: Decompose the goal 'farmers get paid on time' into subgoals and obstacles and say which one would justify a formal specification.

tasks.title: Draw a goal model with one top goal, four subgoals and two softgoals for a farmer payment service, linking each with AND or OR
Pick which of 6 system parts deserve a formal specification given their risk, and write one invariant in plain logic for the funds transfer
Model the cocoa purchasing chain from farmer to port as a process model with actors, documents and payments and mark three failure points

schedule.title: Validation and prioritisation
schedule.exercise: Inspect a 10-requirement specification with a checklist, record defects by type and prioritise the requirements with MoSCoW.

tasks.title: Inspect a short specification against a checklist and log the defects found by type, severity and location
Rank 12 requirements by MoSCoW and cost-value, then compare the resulting release plan for a fixed budget
Compute analytic hierarchy process weights for six requirements from pairwise comparisons, check consistency and explain any contradictions

schedule.title: Negotiation and estimation
schedule.exercise: Write down the interests behind two conflicting positions and propose a solution that meets both.

tasks.title: Count function points for a small registration app from its inputs, outputs, files and queries, and convert them to effort
Resolve a conflict between a security officer and a field agent over login steps using a win-win approach and be scored on the outcome
Chair a review meeting with disagreeing stakeholders, record decisions and open issues and be scored on balance and traceable outcomes

schedule.title: Managing and documenting requirements
schedule.exercise: Build a small traceability matrix for 8 requirements and assess the impact of one change on design, code and tests.

tasks.title: Build a traceability matrix linking eight requirements to design elements and test cases, and spot the unlinked ones
Act as a change control board for five change requests, assess impact and cost and be scored on your accept or reject rulings
Assemble a specification outline following ISO 29148 for a school records system and populate it with 20 attributed requirements

schedule.title: Requirements for African contexts
schedule.exercise: List the constraints a user with a feature phone and an unreliable power supply puts on a savings app, and turn them into requirements.

tasks.title: Turn six field observations about power cuts and cheap phones into measurable non-functional requirements
Design a USSD menu flow diagram for checking balance and sending money with no more than four steps per task
Specify an offline-first sync for a health data app with conflict rules, data budget and recovery, and draw the flow for a clash of two edits

schedule.title: Inclusion, security, safety and capstone
schedule.exercise: Review the capstone specification with a peer for traceability, privacy and inclusion gaps, then revise it.

tasks.title: Check an app's screens against accessibility criteria and write six requirements for contrast, text size, labels and navigation
Draw misuse cases for a mobile wallet showing three attackers and their abuse paths, and add a security requirement that stops each
Produce a validated, traceable specification for a local organisation with at least 30 requirements, privacy and consent clauses and a review record
